76780.subject: 🔷 The Daily: $70 million bitcoin theft
76780.body:
|Galaxy Research estimates $70 million bitcoin theft as Coinkite warns users|Strategy posts $8.2 billion Q2 loss|Tether's excess reserves fall by $4.1 billion|New York sues Kalshi|Uniswap launches Earn

The Daily ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by Yogita Khatri | Edited by Kyle Baird

Happy Friday! Yogita here, filling in for James, with the latest from the crypto world.

Bitcoin hardware wallet maker *Coinkite* warned that some older *Coldcard Mk3 devices may be at risk* following a security incident. According to *Galaxy Research* , about 1,083 BTC, worth roughly *$70 million* , was drained from 1,196 wallets in a 41-minute window, around 30 hours before Coinkite issued its public warning.

Crypto earnings are also in focus. *Strategy* reported an $8.2 billion Q2 loss even as it continued to accumulate bitcoin, while *Coinbase* ( https://www.theblock.co/post/410316/coinbase-q2-miss-sparks-split-wall-street-analysts-debate-growth-beyond-trading?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) shares fell after it reported a loss of $359.5 ⁠million in Q2, and *Tether* 's excess reserves fell by $4.1 billion in Q2.

Regulatory developments also remain in focus. *New York sued Kalshi* over alleged illegal gambling, while *Senate Democrats* *proposed* ( https://www.theblock.co/post/410260/senate-democrat-anti-corruption-bureau?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) a new anti-corruption bureau as scrutiny of President Trump's crypto ties continued.

Meanwhile, *Circle* secured ( https://www.theblock.co/post/410275/circle-secures-nydfs-trust-charter-adding-state-layer-to-federal-usdc-oversight?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) a New York trust charter, and *Uniswap* launched ( https://www.theblock.co/post/410286/uniswap-morpho-earn-yield-gauntlet-vaults?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) a new yield product with *Morpho*.

*P.S.* Don't forget to check out The Funding ( https://www.theblock.co/post/409690/are-crypto-vaults-funds-curators-fund-managers?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) , a biweekly newsletter of crypto VC trends. It's a great read — and just like The Daily , it's free to subscribe ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters?select=The%20Funding&utm_campaign=website&utm_campaign=website&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_medium=referral&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=newsletter&utm_source=newsletter&utm_source=newsletter&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) !

Under normal market conditions, these tools handle routine rebalancing, such as automatically adjusting debt levels to keep constant leverage or smoothly scaling a position’s safety ratio from, for example, 180% to 200%.
However, during a major market selloff between January 25 and February 9, DeFi Saver’s system executed a total of 382 automated repay actions on Aave V3 alone.
Out of these, 95.55% were critical interventions executed on heavily exposed positions running a Safety ratio of <150% (Health factor of 1.55) - all of which would have faced certain liquidation during the event given the size of the market correction.
So today, in this study, we'll be looking at the 365 at-risk positions managed by DFS Automation between January 25 and February 9. To be more precise, these are Aave V3 positions managed via DeFi Saver, across Ethereum Mainnet, Base, Optimism, and Arbitrum.
